scope: All substantive content of supplied printed pages1 and3; no other pages are proof evidence for this packet.

inventory.content: Finite repeated game t=1,...,T; round convention is one-based.
Adversary selects y_t in [0,1] and keeps it secret until after prediction.
Player selects x_t in [0,1] before observing the current outcome.
Current outcome is revealed, with squared loss (x_t-y_t)^2.
Aim is accurate guessing and defining a winning condition.
inventory.exclusion_reason: Motivation only; no extra mathematical premise.

inventory.locator: Paragraph beginning Let us start, first three sentences
inventory.content: Outcomes are IID from one fixed distribution on [0,1], chosen by the adversary at the beginning and unknown to the learner.
If the distribution were known, its mean could be predicted every round for expected loss sigma^2 T; source asserts that one cannot do better.
Expected cumulative squared prediction loss minus sigma^2 T. Expectation subscript names Y_1,...,Y_T, not a separate private seed.
Average expected cumulative loss divided by T minus sigma^2; presented as equivalent normalization for positive T.
Both excess criteria are asserted nonnegative; no probability decomposition is displayed.
Variance normalizes difficulty and the criterion is described as reasonable rather than unique.
inventory.exclusion_reason: Interpretation, not a proof step or additional condition.

inventory.content: Success defined as sublinear total excess or equivalently average excess tending to zero. This is a criterion, not universal success of an arbitrary learner.
